patch_description: The current algorithm routes every partition along the same single shortest path per destination, causing redundant transfers over shared edges and ignoring multi-network parallel paths. A much cheaper broadcast structure is a two-level overlay: (1) build a minimum-cost Steiner-like multicast tree from src to all destinations at the *aggregate* level using shortest-path distances (this shares links, so the data is sent over each tree edge only once instead of num_partitions times), and (2) assign each partition a different parallel path (k shortest node/edge-disjoint paths) so load is balanced across networks and no single bottleneck link carries all partitions. This reduces total cost both by multicast sharing (avoiding redundant src->relay transfers) and by spreading partitions across disjoint low-cost routes.
